raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Automated benchmark artifact refresh.

cuDNN backend: 9.28.0.45
cudnn-frontend commit: 5f15ca77ad3bd47c8ffb5070c6d0ab436120fe56

Includes attention_training, attention_inference, dsa, linear_attention and cutedsl_fusion_kernels benchmark artifacts for gb200, gb300, h200, a100 and rtxpro6000 (dsa: gb200/gb300/h200; linear_attention and cutedsl: gb200/gb300).

Also includes a one-hunk fix to `benchmark/attention_inference/charts.py`: the serving-form cases widened some inference figures past the WebP 16383-px limit at the fixed 140 dpi, so three charts per GPU (deepseek_v4 and gpt_oss generation, prefill_sweep context) failed to save. The dpi is now scaled down just enough to fit; the charts in this refresh were produced with that fix.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

@@ -191,7 +191,14 @@ def _plot_phase(df, config, phase: str, outdir: Path) -> List[Path]:
     fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.96))
     fig.subplots_adjust(hspace=0.55)
     path = outdir / f"{config.name}_{phase}.webp"
-    fig.savefig(path, dpi=140, pil_kwargs={"lossless": True, "quality": 100, "method": 6, "exact": True})
+    # WebP hard-caps both image dimensions at 16383 px. The serving-form cases
+    # (paged / partial-fill clusters) grew some figures past 117 in wide, which
+    # at the fixed 140 dpi exceeds the cap and savefig raises — the chart is
+    # lost while the CSV survives. Scale dpi down just enough to fit: every
+    # element scales with the figure, so relative legibility is unchanged.
+    fig_h = 3.9 * len(row_keys)
+    dpi = min(140, int(16300 // max(fig_w, fig_h)))
+    fig.savefig(path, dpi=dpi, pil_kwargs={"lossless": True, "quality": 100, "method": 6, "exact": True})
     plt.close(fig)
     return [path]
